decisions.id: Stop-time refusal brought back (DECISION, reverses T183's D10)
decisions.summary: A Stop guard blocks the coordinating session's turn end while a pool tree is free, the count is not reached, and a queue holds a READY entry that overlaps nothing in flight; it names the one command, and its escape is POOL_IDLE_OK on a line of its own.
decisions.why: The GM asked on 2026-11-26 for the tooling to 'actually enforce' keeping tasks in flight, and request.md line 13 asks for 'real enforcement and not just instructions'. The Stop check itself comes from the session's line (request.md 460-463), not from the GM. The rule the GM approved on 2026-11-23 was that Stop hooks block only for what the session must do before stopping. Handing a free tree to a READY task is that kind of work. The incident behind that rule, a block firing while the session correctly waited under a hold, is covered by the quiet cases: waits=GM is written once in the file, every entry waiting is quiet, an unreadable queue is quiet, and the escape is recorded. This adds enforcement and narrows nothing.

T88's failure case, a ruling that held new work, is met by waits=GM written once per hold in the file (per entry, as the block states it: a one-time edit, not an answer at every Stop), or by the recorded escape the falsifier counts. Not the per-Stop cost of T88's 23 turns.

decisions.why: A design choice inside the request. Note: the block states 'The GM is weighing whether the primary session becomes a pure orchestrator' as fact, but request.md marks it as 'the session's report of it, not his words'.

decisions.summary: built = count of done lines for the task down to the entry; the known misfires are left to T416
decisions.why: The block itself states two wrong outcomes of the new mechanism. (1) A second builder-done run for one entry (a builder at its cap and its successor) makes the task's NEXT entry read built while it was never dispatched. The tooling then silently fails to keep that task in flight, and the session has to remember it: the exact failure the GM's words name. (2) One run ending two entries leaves the later one READY after the carry, so the new guard refuses a Stop for a dispatch already made. That is a check refusing correct work, and a block for something the session need not do, against the 2026-11-23 limit. This is a defect this task introduces in its own guard, not a pre-existing one. The stated reason for leaving it ('changes make builder-done's log line and every reader of it') is cost. It is not impossibility, not implied by the GM's words, and not needed for the purpose. FR-009's why/id/order is the form a deferral must take, not a ground that makes one legitimate. Fix it here (the block's own priced cure: the done line names the entry it ends), or show the misfire cannot arise under how dispatches are made.

decisions.summary: next = the first READY entry in file order; the Stop block and builder-done step 1 name it, with no regard to FR-013

This guard is a new Stop hook that names the next task to start, and the block neither names FR-013 nor says how its choice honors it. Under file order it names a non-performance entry ahead of an open performance task whenever the hand-written order puts one there. The general rule is not impossible here (next can prefer a READY performance entry), is not implied away by any GM words, and does not defeat the request. State how the named entry satisfies FR-013/SC-006: next prefers an open performance task's READY entry while one exists, or the section shows (measured) why the queue's order already guarantees it.

decisions.summary: next offers, among READY non-overlapping entries, the first naming an open performance task (set_down_hooks::performance), else file order; the measurement clause is read through the [perf] tag
decisions.why: This implements FR-013 for entries that have a line. It uses the same test as make task-start's refusal and the Stop hook. The GM's 2026-11-26 queue ordering is kept within each class.

decisions.summary: An open performance task with no queue.txt line is never offered; the queue's next entry, the Stop block and builder-done's notice name non-performance work while such tasks are open. Left as T421
decisions.why: FR-013 says 'Performance work goes first, in every feature' (the GM 2026-11-20: 'can we in general priotitize performance improvements going forward?'). SC-006 says every Stop-hook 'start the next' names an open performance task while one exists. This plan cites FR-013 under SC-006 for its own ordering, so FR-013 reaches next. The plan's own observation is that no open [perf] task has a queue line. So the case left out is the live case: today every block and every builder-done notice names non-performance work. Performance-first then rests on the session remembering to write those lines, which is exactly the remembering the GM's T313 words were against. The stated reason ('an entry needs a kind and its crates or files, which only its author can write') explains why code cannot dispatch such a task. It does not explain leaving undone the notice the item itself names as the cure. Nor does it explain why the block and the notice name a non-performance dispatch without mentioning the open performance task. Required: when an open performance task (FR-013's test, any active feature) has no queue line, the Stop block, builder-done's step 1 and make builder-next name that task first, with the make queue-add command that writes its entry, rather than offering a non-performance entry silently. A performance task that waits gets its line with waits=<what>, and the guard is then quiet about it. Red first like the others. Not assumed: that make builder-brief passes through make task-start's refusal. The bundle does not show it, and the block's own command is what gets acted on.

decisions.summary: make builder-done's step 1 reads the done task's own feature's queue and prefers performance work within it alone ('the limit, said here')
decisions.why: FR-013's ordering holds 'in any active feature'. The plan's idle() already reads every queue for that reason. builder-done's notice is what the session acts on first, when a tree frees. The any-queue Stop rule catches the miss only while the tree stays free, and acting on the notice ends that. The plan gives no reason for the limit and files no task for it. None of the legitimacy grounds is shown: it is not impossible (idle() already walks every queue), it is not implied by the GM's words, and the literal rule does not defeat the purpose. Required: builder-done's step 1 applies the same any-queue performance preference as idle(), naming a performance entry of another active feature's queue before its own feature's first pick, or the limit is removed by the D-perf-no-line fix.
